title: Derived function complexes for module presheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small ordinary category and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, with sizes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$; kernels and cokernels are objectwise. Use cochains, shifts and quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ be the enhanced localization at objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, retaining derived mapping complexes and coherent mapping spaces [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $T\in\mathcal C$, define the free module presheaf $L_T(V)=\Lambda[\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)]$, where $\Lambda[X]$ is the direct sum of copies of $\Lambda$ indexed by the set $X$.

For any bounded-above complex $A$ in $\mathcal P$ whose terms are small coproducts of the $L_T$, and any possibly unbounded complex $G$, the ordinary complex of presheaf maps computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(A,G)$. This complex has degree $r$ term $\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(A^p,G^{p+r})$ and differential $h\mapsto d_Gh-(-1)^r h d_A$. The comparison is natural in maps between these source complexes and in $G$.

For arbitrary complexes $X,G$, choose a cochain-complex model for $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X,G)$. The derived mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathbf D(\mathcal P)}(X,G)$ is represented, naturally in the enhanced homotopy theory, by the simplicial abelian group obtained by Dold--Kan from the nonnegative chain complex with degree $m>0$ term $(R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X,G))^{-m}$ and degree zero term the degree-zero cycles of $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X,G)$. In particular $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}(X,G)=H^0R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X,G)$ and $\pi_m\operatorname{Map}(X,G)=H^{-m}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X,G)$ for $m\ge1$, at the zero map. Translation gives the same identifications at other basepoints. Under these comparisons, a precomposition map of mapping spaces is an equivalence if and only if its maps on all the nonpositive cohomology groups of derived Hom are isomorphisms. Here Dold--Kan is the equivalence between nonnegative chain complexes and simplicial modules, with normalized chains as inverse. The shift convention gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X[k],G)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X,G)[-k]$ for every $k\in\mathbf Z$, compatibly with precomposition.

source.place: Choudhury--Gallauer Alves de Souza, Homotopy theory of dg sheaves, arXiv:1511.02828v1, Facts 2.3 and 2.8, Example 3.8, Facts 3.10 and 3.14, Lemma 3.16 and Corollary 3.17, printed pp. 5-6, 10-12; convert chain degree n to cochain degree -n. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag in the supplied DAG states this enhanced result.

proof.text: For a presheaf $F$, evaluation on the generator $[\mathrm{id}_T]$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(L_T,F)$ with $F(T)$: the inverse sends $x\in F(T)$ to the map $[u:V\to T]\mapsto F(u)(x)$, extended $\Lambda$-linearly. The two composites are identities by naturality. Consequently $L_T$ has the lifting property against an objectwise surjection, since $x$ lifts in $F(T)$. A map from $\bigoplus_iL_{T_i}$ is a family of such elements; lift each independently and use the coproduct property. Choice and smallness are allowed by the fixed universes. Hence every term of $A$ is projective. This proves the required free-presheaf assertion without a new lemma.

source.place: Example 3.8, printed p. 10; explicit free-module evaluation and lifting argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] to the abelian category $\mathcal P$ and to $A$. Its projective-term hypothesis was proved in Step 1, and boundedness above is a hypothesis of the item. Thus the ordinary Hom complex from $A$ into every objectwise acyclic complex is acyclic. In this presheaf category acyclicity is objectwise because kernels and cokernels are objectwise. This is precisely homotopical projectivity, and imposes no boundedness on the target.

source.place: Fact 3.10, printed p. 10 (chain convention); existing Mathlib K-projective criterion in cochain convention.

proof.text: Form the small dg category $\mathcal B$ with the objects of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal B(U,V)=\Lambda[\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(U,V)]$ in degree zero, viewed over $\mathbf Z$, with bilinear composition. Right dg $\mathcal B$-modules are exactly presheaves of cochain complexes of $\Lambda$-modules: the action of $\lambda[\mathrm{id}_U]$ gives the scalar action and the action of $[u:U\to V]$ gives restriction; the module axioms give their commutation and functoriality. Conversely these formulas define the action. Graded module maps are exactly graded $\Lambda$-linear presheaf maps, so their degree $r$ term is $\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X^p,G^{p+r})$ with differential $d_Gh-(-1)^rhd_X$. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution] to $\mathcal B$: it gives homotopically projective replacements $QX\to X$ for arbitrary $X$, the dg presentation of the enhanced localization, and the derived Hom model $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(QX,G)$. For the homotopically projective $A$ of Step 2 its stated comparison permits $A$ itself as source. This proves the first clause, including naturality in actual maps between the specified sources and in $G$, by the comparison theorem's composition compatibility.

source.place: Lemma 3.16 and Corollary 3.17, printed p. 12; dg-module presentation supplied by the cited generic theorem.

proof.text: For arbitrary $X,G$, take homotopically projective replacements $QX,QG$ from Step 3. The full dg category of these projectives presents $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ by [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution]. Apply the generic simplicial realization of [lem-cbc-dold-kan-homology] to this dg category (it is small after enlarging the universe). Its mapping simplicial modules are $S(E)$ with $E=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(QX,QG)$; that realization is locally Kan and realizes the underlying enhanced category. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], these mapping simplicial sets represent the right-pinched mapping spaces of its coherent nerve, naturally and compatibly with composition. Finally $QG\to G$ induces a quasi-isomorphism on Hom complexes from $QX$: its cone is the Hom complex into the acyclic cone of $QG\to G$ and is acyclic by homotopical projectivity. Thus this $E$ is a model of the same derived Hom as in Step 3. Taking this Hom complex as the chosen cochain-complex model of $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X,G)$ gives the stated mapping-space model rather than assuming it from the homotopy-group calculation. The same representation holds for any other cochain-complex model $E'$, that is, a complex of modules over the coefficient ring $R$ ($R=\mathbf Z$ or $\Lambda$) isomorphic to $E$ in the derived category of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution] to the one-object dg category $R$: it gives a homotopically projective $q:PE'\to E'$, and since its Hom complexes compute the localization, the composite isomorphism $PE'\to E'\cong E$ in the derived category is the class of a closed degree-zero map $g:PE'\to E$. As the cohomology functors factor through the localization, $g$ and $q$ are quasi-isomorphisms, so by the weak-equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-dold-kan-homology] the zigzag $S(E')\leftarrow S(PE')\to S(E)$ consists of weak homotopy equivalences.

source.place: Construction 1.3.1.13 and Proposition 1.3.1.17, printed pp. 83–85; generic dg realization and the existing coherent-nerve comparison.

proof.text: The normalized chains of $S(E)$ are $t(E)$ by [lem-cbc-dold-kan-homology], and that node identifies its homotopy groups with $H^{-m}(E)$, including $m=0$. The degree-zero cycles in $t(E)_0$ are essential: its degree-zero homology is $Z^0(E)/d_E(E^{-1})=H^0(E)$, while its positive homology is $H^{-m}(E)$. Translation by a vertex carries that vertex to zero; composition with a fixed source map is a homomorphism of the simplicial abelian group models, so translation treats every basepoint. The natural comparisons in Step 4 identify precomposition with these maps in the enhanced homotopy theory. The weak-equivalence criterion in the same node is therefore exactly the asserted criterion on all nonpositive cohomology groups.

source.place: Fact 3.14(3)–(4), printed p. 11; good truncation and translation.

proof.text: Write the shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] as $(X[k])^p=X^{p+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}=(-1)^kd_X$. On the ordinary Hom complexes the map $F_r:\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X[k],G)^r\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,G)[-k]^r$ is $(F_rh)^q=(-1)^{kr}h^{q-k}$. For the $d_G$ term the signs in $F_{r+1}d$ and $dF_r$ are both $(-1)^{kr+k}$; for the $hd_X$ term they are both $-(-1)^{kr+r}$. Thus $F$ is a chain isomorphism. It commutes with precomposition by a degree-zero cochain map because the scalar depends only on $k,r$. The same formula shows shifts preserve homotopical projectivity, since shifting an acyclic Hom complex preserves acyclicity. Hence $QX[k]\to X[k]$ is an admissible replacement in Step 3; apply $F$ there to get $R\operatorname{Hom}(X[k],G)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}(X,G)[-k]$. Its compatibility with precomposition descends from the displayed equality and the composition-compatible comparison of Step 3.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain; explicit Hom shift sign computation. The shift convention is also stated by the cited abstract-derived-category definition.
